intended_object: The set of isomorphism classes of countable (finite or countably infinite) models of an L_{ω₁ω} sentence φ in a countable relational language. It is represented through codes: models with universe ℕ, plus models with universe Fin n for each n. This comes from the docstring and from its use in the combined counting dichotomy (`allCodedIsoClasses_dichotomy`).
explanation:
The body is the disjoint union of two parts: the quotient of the coded ℕ-models of φ by isomorphism (`isoSetoid φ`), and the Σ over n of the quotients of the coded Fin n-models of φ by isomorphism (`isoSetoidOn φ n`). In both setoids, two codes are related exactly when the structures they decode to are L-isomorphic.

Every countable structure is isomorphic to one on ℕ or on some Fin n. Structures on different carriers (ℕ, Fin n, Fin m with n ≠ m) have carriers of different cardinality, so they are never isomorphic. The disjoint union therefore lists each isomorphism class of countable models of φ exactly once. This is the standard descriptive-set-theoretic way to code countable models; the counting theorem is about the cardinality of this set.

The degenerate tier Fin 0 holds the empty structure, which is a legitimate structure for a relational language, so it is right to include it.

Nothing in Mathlib is more general: Mathlib has no infinitary logic and no space of codes for countable structures. The countable relational language is the natural setting for this coding. The definition matches its docstring.
